title: A localization of a normal domain is a normal domain with the same fraction field (Stacks 00GY)
statement: Let $R$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with field of fractions $K$, and let $S\subseteq R$ be a multiplicative subset with $0\notin S$. Then $S^{-1}R$ is a normal domain, and the map $S^{-1}R\to K$, $r/s\mapsto r/s$, is injective and identifies $K$ with the field of fractions of $S^{-1}R$. (In particular, for $f\in R$, $f\neq0$, $R_f$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K$, and for a prime $\mathfrak p$, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K$.)
